description: PowerOutageHistory is a website that presents 12 years of US county power outage data, 2014 to 2025, which it says comes from the Department of Energy, for 3,046 counties. Visitors look up a county or ZIP code and see outage history with a reliability grade; the home page reports an average outage duration of 3.0 hours per event nationally, 604 high-risk counties graded F, Nebraska as the top-performing state and state-by-state average grades, for example Arizona A and Florida D. The site also recommends a right-sized generator for each county's outage history, so it has a commercial purpose. Access: free to browse without registration; the page credits the underlying ORNL EAGLE-I outage data as CC BY 4.0 and states no licence of its own, and no download route or method note was found on the page read. Coverage is the United States at county level. Caveats: this is a derived, commercial presentation of DOE data, the grading method is not documented on the home page, and the underlying EAGLE-I records should be used for research. It suits resilience and capacity planning screening of outage exposure by county, and it relates to the PowerOutage.com and EAGLE-I county outage records catalogued here.
